scope: Primary scientific sources for animal/timeline/fossil metadata, not source-video Archetype research or authority for fantasy bonuses.

sources.title: National Museum of Australia — Extinction of thylacine
sources.support: Recently extinct marsupial; skeleton material; last known captive individual died in 1936.

sources.title: Natural History Museum — Dodo facts
sources.support: Recently extinct bird with preserved/subfossil bones.

sources.title: AMNH — Plio-Pleistocene
sources.support: Pleistocene context for Smilodon, Mammuthus, dire wolf, Megatherium, Glyptodon and woolly rhino; group placement, not exact specimen age.

sources.title: AMNH — Oligocene
sources.support: Oligocene giant hornless rhino shown under historical Indricotherium terminology.

sources.title: Deng et al. — An Oligocene giant rhino provides insights into Paraceratherium evolution
sources.support: Primary research on Paraceratherium; same paper accessible from Rhino Resource Center at https://rhinoresourcecenter.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/1624346446.pdf.

sources.title: AMNH — Equoidea
sources.support: Eocene Eohippus in true horse family; do not treat the restricted Hyracotherium genus as a duplicate alias outcome.

sources.title: Smithsonian — World’s largest snake discovered in fossilized rainforest
sources.support: Titanoboa vertebrate fossil bones in 58–60 million-year-old deposits; Paleocene.

sources.title: NHM — Late Cretaceous Dino Directory
sources.support: Lists Tyrannosaurus, Triceratops, Ankylosaurus, Velociraptor and Spinosaurus in Late Cretaceous.

sources.title: NHM — Tyrannosaurus
sources.support: Late Cretaceous and bone-bearing large predatory dinosaur.

sources.title: NHM — Ankylosaurus
sources.support: Late Cretaceous, bony body armour and tail club.

sources.title: NHM — What is a mosasaur?
sources.support: Late Cretaceous marine reptile with fossil bones; not a dinosaur.

sources.title: NHM — Stegosaurus
sources.support: Late Jurassic, bony plates and tail spikes.

sources.title: NHM — Brachiosaurus
sources.support: Late Jurassic large sauropod; distinct from Giraffatitan, not extra alias weight.

sources.title: AMNH — Coelophysis
sources.support: Late Triassic, small early theropod with preserved skeletons.

sources.title: Smithsonian — Dimetrodon specimen
sources.support: Early Permian synapsid; skull/vertebra/rib cage in collection.

sources.title: AMNH — Dimetrodon
sources.support: Synapsid and early mammal relative; sail functions are uncertain, so no factual thermal-control ability is asserted.

exclusions: Do not assert exact age for a generated specimen from the chosen animal alone.
Do not classify Mosasaurus or Dimetrodon as dinosaurs.
Do not call Paramecium a bone-bearing extinct animal.
Do not use sharks/invertebrates as bone discoveries without an explicit teeth/exoskeleton/fossil expansion.
